Jazz pianist Håkan Rydin was born in Gislaved, Sweden on January 4, 1951. He led the Nexus Trio from 1972-92, touring the globe and producing critically acclaimed recordings. He has performed with numerous American jazz artists in Europe and he is currently Professor of Jazz Piano at the Malmö Academy of Music at Lund University.
Håkan was interviewed in Glasgow, Scotland on July 27, 2016 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Glasgow with Håkan Rydin.
Very good. In fact much better than I’m used to, but — it’s often “Hakan,” but it’s [sounds like] Hoken in Swedish.
Yeah. You’ve gotten a lot of variations on that.

Yes. I was performing in the Montreal festival and it was a recording for the radio. And there was a guy who was going to introduce us and he really wanted it correctly. So he spent a lot of time on our Swedish names. And he was pretty nervous about it. And he took notes. It was a French guy, French Canadian. And when he came on to the stage he said, “On piano, [speaks fast] akan redin.” But that’s fine.
